about: Exo identity spec v0 (plan §2; §2.14 lists what changed in /2, §2.15 in /3, §2.16 in /4). Bytes are lowercase hex unless a field says otherwise; JSON records are as they travel. Every signature is low-s. HPKE itself is checked against RFC 9180 A.3.1.

base32Refused.why: no whole number of bytes has this length

exceptInEmoji.joiner: U+200D only between two pictographs; the one before may also be U+FE0F
exceptInEmoji.selectors: U+FE0E and U+FE0F only right after a pictograph or a keycap base
exceptInEmoji.tags: U+E0020 to U+E007E only right after U+1F3F4 or another of them, and right before another of them or U+E007F
exceptInEmoji.cancelTag: U+E007F only right after one of U+E0020 to U+E007E

refused.name: 😀‍
refused.why: a joiner with no pictograph after it

refused.name: ‍😀
refused.why: a joiner with nothing before it

refused.name: ️PC
refused.why: a variation selector with nothing before it

refused.name: 🏴󠁧󠁢 PC
refused.why: a flag's tags not ended by U+E007F

deriveScalar.note: a sync key whose sync box needs a second candidate

refused.why: no v or app (the old vector's shape)
an unknown field in the batch
an unknown field in an item
an unknown field in place of body
a v this reader doesn't know (a new field comes with a new v)

recovery.kitIs: a kind 0x02 envelope to sealPublicKey (the entry's encPub), mailbox id boxId, signed by the PC that posts it (by)
recovery.headerEpochIs: the recovery box's own key counter: the code's number, 1 for the identity's first code (deviceList adds this one first), one more for each after it; not the sync-key epoch in the kit (3)

refusedKits.why: header epoch 0: no code number (the /3 form)
header epoch 3: the kit's sync-key epoch, not its code's number (1)

cases.rule: 1. a remove beats any concurrent change by the device it removes
cases.head: 34915df6b23534611e7640abca842211c6ac28c16dcb7a9a4e9202cd29f155f2

cases.rule: 2. two devices remove each other: the one added earlier wins, so a stolen PC added first beats a newer one (the recovery code takes it back: case 6)
cases.head: 34915df6b23534611e7640abca842211c6ac28c16dcb7a9a4e9202cd29f155f2

cases.rule: 3. otherwise the lower hash wins; the loser's author signs it again on top with the next seq and the new head as prev, keeping its at
cases.head: 8630b700599638c289f5a58ae45fa7709f93ef53d7d02a0d34007b56ba105485

cases.rule: 4. a three-way cycle (pairwise: A's remove beats B's rename, B's beats C's by hash, C's beats A's by hash): B is struck, then the lower hash of what's left; the losers are signed again in rank order, so A's remove of B goes first and B's rename is dropped
cases.head: 084829cb64986d6716905b337defa23d78bb9e0bd6f4c5fd5ccba6fecb1f0bda

cases.rule: 5. four at once (B and A remove each other, C renames, D removes C): A strikes B, D strikes C, then the lower hash of A's and D's; in rank order A's remove of B is signed again first, so B's remove of A (lower hash) is dropped
cases.head: 18c4715fae899d7d30cd520719639892c4e31ccd33179c93b44bf7491a299b19

cases.rule: 6. the recovery code in the race of case 2: it ranks before every PC, so its remove strikes A (the stolen PC added first) and the lower hash of R's and B's wins
cases.head: 0ea4018f5a5e9eccd77588745635cbc55f3dc1268c83284a4ff6ed36b22fe9f1

droppedOnResign.why: the device it removes is gone

cases.rule: 7. a losing branch of three is signed again in order by its author, each change keeping its content and at; one that no longer applies (it renames C, which the winner removed) is dropped and the rest go on
cases.head: 72c990b6838b78306611db2c24b92bd82fa538b0134d8ea1a34ae3acf74c8eed

droppedOnResign.why: the device it renames is gone

cases.rule: 8. two losers that still apply, by different authors: each is signed again on top of the new head in its author's rank order, one after another (B's, then C's on top of it), whatever their hashes or arrival order
cases.head: 03a7bd3d40e19123c2960230c144afe4763a2f35e9a98a96cf8548bdff7d9216

cases.rule: 9. equivocation: C signs two different changes after the same head; whoever sees both drops both (in either order) and marks C, which stays listed; D's change wins, and C's next change at a higher seq counts again
cases.head: e15e4e25dc5aec0c7d2c61b654288c8a3d7d290b5dcbd438668cbc0a2a170847

deviceListAccepted.why: the recovery entry removes itself: recovery off (only the code may)
a PC removes itself: it leaves the identity

deviceListRefused.why: a PC removes the recovery entry (only the code turns recovery off)
a PC adds a second recovery entry (only the code replaces its own)
the recovery entry renames a device
a PC renames the recovery entry (no one renames it)
a name with a zero-width space
a field a change doesn't have
a device record with "recovery": false (the flag is there only as true)
